downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: For a protocol of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], fix a bath temperature $T_b>0$ kelvin and set $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T_b)^{-1}$ in joules$^{-1}$, using the exact constant and SI conventions of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The finite-state clause of the adopted [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] then gives the stage-zero law $\pi_0(i)=e^{-\beta E_0(i)}/Z_0$; adopt that the initial microstate is drawn from this law, so $\mu_0=\pi_0$. Here $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and $E_0(i)$ is finite, so $0<Z_0<\infty$ as required by that clause. This is a model premise about the preparation distribution. It does not follow from the finite partition-sum definition, does not assert that an arbitrary system equilibrates in finite time, and does not report a measured preparation. The countable-state and measure-integral branches of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] are not used.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: For the protocol in [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], adopt, at each stage $k=1,\ldots,m$, the stationarity condition $\sum_{i\in\Omega}\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)$ for every $j\in\Omega$. This says that if the bath transition begins with law $\pi_k$ at fixed energy $E_k$, it ends with the same law. It is a physical modeling assumption for this protocol family, not a consequence of the transition-kernel definition and not an assertion that the kernel mixes every initial law to $\pi_k$.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: Assume the setup of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], the canonical initial law of [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]], the stationarity model of [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]], and, additionally, $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$ for every $k,i,j$. For every forward path with positive probability, define its reverse probability by $P_R(\omega^R)=\pi_m(i_m)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$. Then $P_R(\omega^R)>0$ and $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=e^{\beta(W(\omega)-\Delta F)}$. Consequently, at each work value $w$, $P_F(W=w)=e^{\beta(w-\Delta F)}P_R(W_R=-w)$. The reverse protocol first applies the stage-$k$ reverse transition at fixed $E_k$, then reverses the quench $E_k\to E_{k-1}$; its work is $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$.
